sources.title: Adaptive-WAM: Quality-Guided Early-Exit Planning from Intermediate Video-Diffusion Features

sectionsRead: Title, authors, abstract and version statement

Appendix H.1–H.3 scorer architecture and diagnostics
omissions: Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
The extraction limitation was addressed by inspecting original PDF pages 1–7 and 10–17 and all five final crops; reference-only pages 8–9 were read as text.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
Code and external linked resources were not inspected; no experiments were reproduced.

Identity scope: the supplied title page verifies arXiv:2608.06008v1, 6 August 2026, with all three catalog authors. No title/author discrepancy or different edition was observed; no other revision was supplied.

synopsis: Adaptive-WAM turns a video-diffusion backbone into a driving planner that stops when an intermediate trajectory looks adequate. Video prediction shapes training; deployment uses one conditional feature pass and a separate quality verifier. Its adaptive result is 90.79 PDMS at 170 ms, while the higher 92.6 score belongs to a different fixed-exit, 64-proposal system.

problem.text: Driving requires an ego trajectory, yet video-based planners can inherit expensive future synthesis or a fixed backbone depth. The paper asks whether planning quality can determine how much of a pretrained video model must run, while retaining predictive supervision during learning.

contributions.text: Six comparable action exits expose depth-dependent planning quality. Across five tested video-noise indices, single-trajectory IL varies only 0.13–0.15 PDMS; this supports fixing the tested index, not universal noise invariance.

A separate component-predicting verifier selects when to stop and which accumulated trajectory to return. Partial overlap between high-quality scene sets motivates deeper fallback despite B15 having the strongest average.

inputs: Current/historical ego information and navigation command
Observation-derived text description; future images are training targets only
outputs: Eight ego poses (x, y, heading), at 0.5-second intervals over four seconds
One selected trajectory; no future video is required online

steps.name: Read a conditional video prefix
steps.detail: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B processes the current image and description at index 17 of a 40-step video schedule. The future latent portion starts from scheduler noise, not observed future frames.

steps.name: Decode independent action exits
steps.detail: Blocks 5, 9, 15, 18, 22 and 30 feed separate projections and ReCogDrive-style diffusion heads. Each head conditions on video features, ego state and navigation, then uses five DDIM updates to produce one trajectory.

steps.name: Verify accumulated quality
steps.detail: A fine-tuned DINOv2-Small image encoder and trajectory MLP feed six component heads: no-at-fault collision, drivable-area compliance, driving-direction compliance, time-to-collision, ego progress and comfort. The scorer receives neither ego state nor route command.

steps.name: Continue only when necessary
steps.detail: Cache the best predicted trajectory and continue from the previous hidden state when its score is insufficient. Return the accumulated best at the threshold or at B30. A forced final fallback can return a trajectory from an earlier exit.

training.text: Filter NAVSIM navtrain into 82,555 complete nine-frame clips from 103,288 candidates. Future frames provide four seconds of video supervision. Wan uses 1280×704 images; the scorer uses 832×480. Descriptions use current or historical attributes and cached text embeddings.

During imitation learning, shared Wan LoRA, projections and action heads learn from video and trajectory losses. Base Wan weights and VAE remain frozen. Alternating scorer updates use detached generated trajectories with equal-weight soft-label BCE, preventing scorer gradients from changing the actor.

Planner-only DiffGRPO subsequently freezes Wan and the scorer and updates action heads. Each five-step denoising chain receives evaluator reward; groups contain eight sampled trajectories, with a behavior-cloning term. These training groups are distinct from the one-per-exit inference pool.

inference.text: The deployed pool holds at most six trajectories. Cached-prefix continuation avoids restarting Wan, but every attempted exit still pays for action denoising and scoring. The selected threshold is 90 on a 100-point scale; video classifier-free sampling and future-video decoding are skipped.

Figure 4 shows “Score > Threshold?”, while Eq. (6) discussion and Algorithm 1 specify greater-than-or-equal. This report follows the explicit algorithm. Its future-scene branch and LoRA placements are schematic; LoRA actually spans the backbone.

equations.explanation: Observation o supplies image I and description d(o). The conditional prefix F produces hidden state h at fixed video index s-star = 17. Projection P supplies features to head G; ego state S and navigation command L condition trajectory tau at exit ell.

equations.expression: \hat q_j=\max_{m\le j}Q(\hat r_{\ell_m}),\qquad Q(\hat r)=100\,\Gamma(\hat r),\qquad \hat q_j\ge\eta
equations.explanation: After j attempted exits, q-hat is the best predicted quality; m indexes attempted exits and ell-m denotes their block locations. Predicted metric components r-hat are composed by normalized score Gamma. Eta is the stopping threshold; the associated best trajectory is returned.

The displayed v1 metric multiplies collision and drivable-area terms by weighted progress, time-to-collision and comfort. Its normalized value is multiplied by 100 in reported scores. DDC is predicted by the scorer but absent from this v1 formula.

results.task: NAVSIM v1 adaptive planning and latency
results.setting: Navtest, front camera without LiDAR; one trajectory per attempted exit; threshold 90; A100 80GB, batch one.
results.value: 90.79 PDMS (90.8 rounded); 170 ms; 94.1% exit by B15.
results.comparison: Fixed B15: 90.62 / 190 ms; full path: 85.82 / 320 ms.
results.interpretation: The gain over B15 is 0.17 points with about 10% lower mean latency. The full path additionally decodes once; the 47% reduction is not an isolated depth-only comparison.

results.setting: Fixed B22, 64 proposals, separate decoder and pseudo-expert coverage training; no adaptive routing.
results.interpretation: The higher score changes decoder, supervision and proposal budget; it cannot be credited to adaptive exits or paired with 170 ms.

results.setting: Official navtest EPDMS protocol; single front camera, no LiDAR.
results.interpretation: Best among the listed world-model planners. V2 uses different components and two-stage aggregation, so its scale is not interchangeable with v1.

results.setting: No nuScenes fine-tuning; averages over 1, 2 and 3 seconds.
results.interpretation: Transfer is competitive but does not lead these two averages; it is not evidence of physical closed-loop driving.

results.value: Joint LoRA 90.62; separate LoRA plus cached features 84.95.
results.interpretation: Joint adaptation adds 5.67 points over caching. The 0.02 full-tuning difference has no uncertainty estimate here.

results.setting: Fixed candidate pool spanning 12,146 scenes, separate from adaptive inference.
results.value: 91.2% / 94.4%; 51 cases with at least a 50-point gap.
results.comparison: More than 95% of scenes contain all-perfect, all-zero or top-tied candidates.
results.interpretation: Strong selection accuracy under saturation does not certify safe early stopping on a shifted online pool.

limitations.text: NAVSIM v1 uses non-reactive background actors; v2 approximates feedback with precomputed follow-up scenes. The authors explicitly deny a safety guarantee from the stopping threshold.

Source inconsistencies remain: Appendix F says the auxiliary B18 noise range is 0.14, while displayed extrema imply 0.16; Tables 16–17 show zero diagonal count means with nonzero standard deviations. Neither is silently repaired or used to strengthen a conclusion.

The six-output scorer and displayed v1 composition do not specify how the additional v2 components enter routing. Main result and routing tables provide no confidence intervals for the small adaptive gain.

reproduction.text: Required resources include Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, DINOv2-Small, NAVSIM/OpenScene clips and evaluators. LoRA targets q/k/v/o with rank/alpha/dropout 32/64/0.05; its four-GPU recipe uses effective batch 80 for 80 epochs. Planner IL/GRPO use AdamW at 1e-4, 200/50 epochs and effective batches 1024/32.

Exact internal validation tokens, numerical actor loss weights, full scorer optimizer settings, software versions and coordination of the differing training schedules remain unspecified. Code is promised, not established as released. Timing replication must retain cached text and distinguish the 320 ms planning reference from the separate 13.22 s video-synthesis path.

reasoning.text: Distinct Wan and trajectory-diffusion modules, plus a separately optimized verifier, support Dual-system. Joint video/trajectory supervision is explicit during training, but deployed inference predicts trajectories from video features without jointly generating a visual future or performing inverse dynamics. Thus “Joint prediction” and Q3 need a training-versus-inference qualification; the catalog snapshot is preserved.

discussionQuestions: Does cross-depth routing outperform repeated B15 samples under matched decoding and scoring cost?
Does the verifier preserve its false-accept rate when the scene distribution or candidate pool changes?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title block, arXiv margin and abstract
evidence.detail: The exact catalog title and all three authors match: Sining Ang, Yuguang Yang, Yan Wang. The artifact identifies arXiv:2608.06008v1 [cs.RO], 6 August 2026, and credits AIR, Tsinghua University; USTC Department of Automation; and Beihang School of Electronic Information Engineering. Code is promised for future release.

evidence.location: PDF p. 2, Figure 1 and caption
evidence.detail: Adaptive-WAM uses trajectory exits and quality scoring; future-video prediction supervises training but is unnecessary for deployed planning.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section 3 and Table 1; p. 13, Appendix G.1, Table 14
evidence.detail: Identical single-trajectory head schedules and validation-best selection over ten runs give B15 86.56 IL / 90.62 RL, versus B30 80.71 / 85.82. No PDMS confidence intervals accompany these table entries.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section 3, video timestep analysis; p. 13, Appendix F, Table 13
evidence.detail: Single-trajectory IL scores span 0.13 at B15 and 0.15 at B18 across indices 1, 9, 17, 25, 32. The auxiliary B18 row ranges from 92.43 to 92.59, although adjacent prose calls its range 0.14.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Figure 2; p. 13, Appendix G.2, Eq. (19); p. 14, Table 15
evidence.detail: High-quality scene sets use PDMS at least 90. Mean Jaccard overlap over ten aligned runs ranges from 0.69 to 0.82 off the diagonal; B9/B15 is 0.82 and B15/B30 is 0.73.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 3; p. 14, Appendix G.3, Eq. (20); p. 15, Tables 16–17
evidence.detail: Directional counts concern score advantages of at least 50 points. Post-RL B15 over B30 is 598.64 and the reverse is 422.41. Diagonal means are zero but the displayed standard deviations are nonzero; the paper does not resolve that feature of the paired-run calculation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Section 4, Eqs. (1)–(2); p. 11, Appendices D.1–D.2
evidence.detail: A Wan2.2-TI2V-5B conditional prefix uses the current front image and observation-derived description at video index 17. Scheduler noise initializes the future latent portion. Independent projected heads at blocks 5, 9, 15, 18, 22, 30 each perform five DDIM updates to output eight ego poses.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Section 4, Eqs. (3)–(7); p. 5, Algorithm 1
evidence.detail: The scorer takes an image and trajectory, predicts metric components and maintains the best accumulated predicted score. The controller stops at score greater than or equal to the validation-selected threshold, or at B30, and returns the best accumulated trajectory. Backbone prefixes and scores are reused.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Figure 4 and caption, Algorithm 1 line 9; p. 12, Appendix D.4
evidence.detail: Figure 4 shows a strict greater-than branch, whereas Algorithm 1 uses greater-than-or-equal. The caption labels future-video generation as training supervision and repeated heads/LoRA locations as schematic; Appendix D.4 places LoRA throughout Wan.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Training; pp. 10–11, Appendices C.1–C.3, Table 8
evidence.detail: Temporal filtering retains 82,555 of 103,288 candidates as nine-frame clips at 2 Hz, removing 20,733. Wan images are 1280 by 704; scorer images are 832 by 480. Descriptions use anchor-time or historical information and cached T5 embeddings. Corpus counts do not specify the internal validation partition.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 5–6, Training, Eqs. (8)–(11); p. 11, Appendix D.3
evidence.detail: Joint video and trajectory losses update Wan LoRA and the projected trajectory heads. Scorer updates alternate with actor updates, using detached trajectories and equal-weight soft-target BCE for six components. Planner-only DiffGRPO freezes Wan and the scorer.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 12–13, Appendix D.4, Tables 10–11 and GRPO paragraph
evidence.detail: Wan LoRA targets q/k/v/o with rank 32, alpha 64, dropout 0.05; its four-GPU recipe uses effective batch 80 for 80 epochs. Planner IL/GRPO schedules are 200/50 epochs with AdamW at 1e-4 and effective batches 1024/32. GRPO groups contain eight samples, with discount 0.6 and behavior-cloning weight 0.1. Numerical actor loss weights, full scorer optimization, software versions and exact schedule coordination are not supplied.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Appendices H.1–H.3, Tables 18–20; p. 17, Appendix M
evidence.detail: DINOv2-Small uses image and flattened trajectory, without ego state or route command. Six heads predict NC, DAC, DDC, TTC, EP and comfort. On a separate 12,146-scene pool, exact/within-five-point selection is 91.2%/94.4%; 51 and 69 scenes have at least 50- and 20-point gaps. DINO-Small selected-candidate score is 92.59 versus Wan-B22 92.62, not end-to-end planner PDMS.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 2, NAVSIM v1 navtest
evidence.detail: Adaptive single-trajectory PDMS is 90.8, fixed-B22 64-proposal PDMS is 92.6, and listed DriveVA PDMS is 90.5. Adaptive NC/DAC/TTC/comfort/EP are 98.6/97.9/95.6/100/85.1; DriveVA values are 99.2/97.5/98.7/100/83.5. C and CL distinguish camera and camera-plus-LiDAR.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 3; p. 10, Appendix B.1, Eqs. (13)–(14)
evidence.detail: NAVSIM v2 navtest reports 89.9 EPDMS for Adaptive-WAM, 86.1 for DriveVLA-W0, 85.1 for Epona and 90.3 for the human agent. The metric uses additional components, human-reference penalty filtering and a two-stage follow-up aggregation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Appendix B.1, Eq. (12)
evidence.detail: NAVSIM v1 evaluates four-second trajectories in non-reactive simulation with recorded background futures and a controller for ego rollout. Its displayed normalized PDMS is NC times DAC times (5 EP + 5 TTC + 2 comfort)/12. V2 approximates closed-loop behavior without interactive simulation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Appendix E and Table 12; p. 13, continuation of Appendix E
evidence.detail: The fixed-B22 comparator uses a separate learned-token decoder with 64 proposals and evaluator-filtered pseudo-expert coverage supervision. Training-time map and future occupancy construct targets; this is distinct from adaptive five-step single-trajectory decoding.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 5; p. 15, Appendix J, Table 23
evidence.detail: At thresholds 70/80/90/95, PDMS is 88.49/90.64/90.79/90.75 and mean latency is 112/143/170/284 ms. At 90, 94.1% stop by B15. Fixed B15 is 90.62 at 190 ms; full path is 85.82 at 320 ms.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 6; p. 15, Appendix I, Tables 21–22
evidence.detail: Single-trajectory scores are 84.20 frozen Wan, 84.95 separate LoRA with caching, 90.62 joint LoRA and 90.64 full tuning. ViT-S/B/L give 83.91/85.62/88.88. The auxiliary 64-proposal columns are separate experiments.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Computation; pp. 15–16, Appendix K, Table 24
evidence.detail: Planning latency uses one A100 80GB at batch one and includes VAE image encoding, conditional Wan prefix, attempted heads and scoring; cached text encoding is excluded. The full-depth reference additionally decodes once. The separate nine-frame, 40-step classifier-free video synthesis path takes 13.22 s, with 80 Wan forwards.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 4; p. 10, Appendix B.2; pp. 16–17, Appendix L, Tables 25–26
evidence.detail: NAVSIM-to-nuScenes zero-shot evaluation averages the 1/2/3-second metrics: Adaptive-WAM L2 0.35/0.71/1.58 m, average 0.88 m; collision 0.00/0.09/0.15%, average 0.08%. DriveVA averages 0.84 m and 0.06%.

evidence.location: PDF p. 17, Appendix M
evidence.detail: The authors state that rare scorer failures matter, stricter thresholds cannot guarantee safety, and a passing quality threshold is not a formal safety certificate.
